blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The constitutional development of India spans from 1773 to 1947.
Early foundational legislative milestones include the Regulating Act, 1773 and Pitt's India Act, 1784.
Three consecutive Charter Acts were enacted in 1813, 1833, and 1853.
The Indian Councils Act, 1909 is specifically identified as the Morley–Minto Reforms.
Major British administrative frameworks were established under the Government of India Acts of 1858, 1919, and 1935.
INTRODUCTION

blocks.content: The Constitution of India is not the result of a single event or a sudden decision. It is the outcome of a long historical process extending over nearly two centuries. During British rule, several constitutional and administrative experiments were introduced to strengthen British control and improve governance in India.

These constitutional developments gradually introduced the concepts of centralized administration, rule of law, representation, federalism and responsible government. A major portion of the present Indian Constitution is based on the Government of India Act, 1935, which makes the study of constitutional development extremely important.
The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first attempt by the British Parliament to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India.

items:
• Governor of Bengal was made Governor-General of Bengal.
  • Lord Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General.
  • An Executive Council of four members was created to assist the Governor-General.
  • A Supreme Court was established at Calcutta in 1774.
  • The Company was required to submit its reports to the British Parliament.
Governor of Bengal was made Governor-General of Bengal.
Lord Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General.
An Executive Council of four members was created to assist the Governor-General.
A Supreme Court was established at Calcutta in 1774.
The Company was required to submit its reports to the British Parliament.

• No clear separation of powers.
  • Conflict between Governor-General and Supreme Court.
  • Inefficient administration and corruption continued.
No clear separation of powers.
Conflict between Governor-General and Supreme Court.
Inefficient administration and corruption continued.

blocks.content: This Act marked the beginning of parliamentary control over Indian administration.
The Pitt‟s India Act was passed to remove the defects of the Regulating Act.

items:
• Introduced the system of Dual Government.
  • Board of Control was created to manage political affairs.
  • Court of Directors controlled commercial functions.
  • British Government became the supreme authority.
Introduced the system of Dual Government.
Board of Control was created to manage political affairs.
Court of Directors controlled commercial functions.
British Government became the supreme authority.

blocks.content: This Act clearly established the supremacy of the British Crown over the Company.
The Charter Act of 1813 renewed the charter of the East India Company for 20 years. Important Provisions:

items:
• Company‟s trade monopoly was abolished except for tea and China trade.
  • Christian missionaries were allowed to work in India.
  • A sum of ₹1 lakh per year was allocated for education.
Company‟s trade monopoly was abolished except for tea and China trade.
Christian missionaries were allowed to work in India.
A sum of ₹1 lakh per year was allocated for education.

blocks.content: This Act marked the beginning of modern education and social reforms in India.
The Charter Act of 1833 was a landmark in the constitutional history of India. Main Provisions:

items:
• The Company ceased to be a commercial body and became a purely administrative body.
  • Governor-General of Bengal became the Governor-General of India.
  • Lord William Bentinck became the first Governor-General of India.
  • A Law Commission was established under Lord Macaulay.
  • Legislative powers were centralized.
The Company ceased to be a commercial body and became a purely administrative body.
Governor-General of Bengal became the Governor-General of India.
Lord William Bentinck became the first Governor-General of India.
A Law Commission was established under Lord Macaulay.
Legislative powers were centralized.

blocks.content: This Act laid the foundation of centralized administration and uniform laws in India.
The Charter Act of 1853 further strengthened British administration. Main Features:

items:
• Open competition for civil services was introduced.
  • Legislative and executive functions were separated.
  • Legislative Council was expanded.
Open competition for civil services was introduced.
Legislative and executive functions were separated.
Legislative Council was expanded.

blocks.content: This Act marked the beginning of a modern and merit-based civil service system.
The Government of India Act, 1858 was passed after the Revolt of 1857. Main Provisions:

items:
• East India Company was abolished.
  • India came under the direct control of the British Crown.
  • Governor-General became the Viceroy.
  • Lord Canning became the first Viceroy.
  • A Secretary of State for India was appointed in Britain.
East India Company was abolished.
India came under the direct control of the British Crown.
Governor-General became the Viceroy.
Lord Canning became the first Viceroy.
A Secretary of State for India was appointed in Britain.

blocks.content: This Act marked the beginning of Crown Rule in India.

items:
• Legislative powers were restored to provincial governments.
  • Portfolio system was introduced.
  • Viceroy was empowered to issue ordinances.
Legislative powers were restored to provincial governments.
Portfolio system was introduced.
Viceroy was empowered to issue ordinances.

blocks.content: It introduced the beginning of representative institutions in India.

items:
• Legislative councils were enlarged.
  • Indirect elections were introduced.
  • Members were allowed to discuss the budget.
Legislative councils were enlarged.
Indirect elections were introduced.
Members were allowed to discuss the budget.

blocks.content: This Act increased Indian participation in administration.

items:
• Separate electorate was introduced for Muslims.
  • Indians were appointed to Executive Councils.
  • Size of legislative councils was increased.
Separate electorate was introduced for Muslims.
Indians were appointed to Executive Councils.
Size of legislative councils was increased.

blocks.content: This Act introduced communal representation in Indian politics.

items:
• Dyarchy was introduced in provinces.
  • Bicameral legislature was established at the Centre.
  • Public Service Commission was created.
  • Extended communal representation.
Dyarchy was introduced in provinces.
Bicameral legislature was established at the Centre.
Public Service Commission was created.
Extended communal representation.

blocks.content: Dyarchy failed due to divided authority and lack of coordination.

items: Remember the key timeline of British constitutional acts spanning from 1773 to 1947.
Note the official alternate name for the Indian Councils Act, 1909: Morley–Minto Reforms.

blocks.content: The Government of India Act, 1935 was the most comprehensive constitutional document before independence.

items:
• Federal system introduced.
  • Provincial autonomy granted.
  • Dyarchy abolished in provinces.
  • Federal Court and Reserve Bank of India established.
  • Provided the basic structure of the Indian Constitution.
Federal system introduced.
Provincial autonomy granted.
Dyarchy abolished in provinces.
Federal Court and Reserve Bank of India established.
Provided the basic structure of the Indian Constitution.

• Ended British rule in India.
  • Created two independent dominions – India and Pakistan.
  • Constituent Assembly became sovereign.
  • Governor-General became a constitutional head.
Ended British rule in India.
Created two independent dominions – India and Pakistan.
Constituent Assembly became sovereign.
Governor-General became a constitutional head.

blocks.content: This Act marked the birth of independent India.

The constitutional developments from 1773 to 1947 laid the foundation of India‟s democratic system. The British introduced administrative, legal and political institutions which later evolved into the framework of the Indian Constitution. These developments ultimately paved the way for India‟s independence and the adoption of the Constitution in 1950.
